title: Predictive capacity hedging and stability slots for release windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: reduce rollout risk and last-minute firefighting by reserving deterministic stability capacity and using predictive hedging ahead of planned launch windows across runtime, console, and API surfaces. This initiative defines a playbook and automation to: 1) forecast per-window load uplift using historical telemetry and feature-flag schedules, 2) allocate "stability slots" (reserved GPU/instance capacity) with guardrails, 3) temporarily relax autoscaler cooldowns and increase burst headroom during cutovers, and 4) wire metric-driven rollback triggers and validation checks. Scope covers hosted/runtime deployments, Dedicated pools, and the Console UI controls for launch owners. Deliverables: predictive model spec, capacity reservation API, runbook with signal thresholds and owners, Console UX for slot booking/visibility, and an operational dashboard for pre-launch readiness checks.
acceptance_criteria: A predictive load model prototype that forecast peak qps and token throughput for a given release window with at least ±15% median error on historical backtests
Capacity reservation API that can lock/unlock a defined pool of capacity for a named release window and surface booking status via Console
Automated pre-launch check that runs 24h and 2h before a window and fails if latency or capacity headroom < configured thresholds
Runbook and on-call roster documented and linked; rollback triggers (error rate, 95th latency, OOMs) codified and tested in a staging shadow run
Console UI shows booked stability slots, remaining headroom, and provides a one-click emergency release of reserved capacity
Playbook validated in a simulated release rehearsal with runtime and Dedicated pools where an intentional canary fails and automatic fallback is exercised
